Guest-arrival alert hover: complete native source boundary

Source: the actual reference and classic PE files configured by
data/runtime/native-pe-images.json. pe-functions.tsv retains their full paths,
PE identities, SHA-256 values and decoded function ranges. The *.c files are
Ghidra decompiler output; *.asm, pe-branches.tsv, pe-conditions.tsv,
pe-literals.tsv and pe-switches.tsv retain the native operands and branches.
This is offline source extraction, not an observation of the running game.

Actual decompiler output retained
  Both images completed Ghidra C export for travellers-producer,
  announcement-submit, report-category, migrant-producer and
  alert-popup-renderer (ten completed native functions in all).
  The complete Fortress main renderer is also retained as original assembly,
  literal operands, switch aliases and branch edges in
  pe-*-fortress-alert-hover-owner.asm and the native TSV inventories. Whole-
  renderer C output was not produced: its broad simplification remained
  running, and the final raw-tree attempt was stopped at task completion.
  That explicit stop yielded the exact Ghidra diagnostic "Decompiler process
  died" at reference 0x3d6950 / classic 0x3d4510 (shell exit 1). This is not
  reported as successful C decompilation. The card-specific producers,
  category membership, report ownership and expanded renderer were already
  fully decompiled; the hover instruction/count branches also remain in the
  complete original machine-code source. The default Java export therefore
  selects the bounded producer chain; the monolithic owner is opt-in.

  A final bounded-region attempt used the actual full renderer CFG to retain
  three related native basic-block regions per image, without treating them
  as independent native functions. pe-hover-regions.tsv identifies their
  parent, range and every original continuation; pe-hover-edges.tsv preserves
  internal, incoming and outgoing edges. pe-*-*-region.asm preserves every
  original instruction byte, and pe-hover-literals.tsv / pe-hover-calls.tsv
  retain the literal and supplier operands. Parent register/stack live-ins
  are external inputs. The Ghidra analysis used boundary continuation stubs
  and an explicit final-fallthrough boundary; it did not patch native bytes.

  Reference parent 0x3d6950, classic parent 0x3d4510:
    alert-button-hover-source-region
      reference [0x3d740d,0x3d7627); classic [0x3d4fcd,0x3d51e7)
      C status: reference timeout; classic timeout.
      Hit bounds, report-vector lookup, repetition suffix, wrapping/colors,
      and hover-card position.
    alert-icon-hover-source-region
      reference [0x3f60da,0x3f6830); classic [0x3f3c9a,0x3f43f0)
      C status: reference not attempted; classic not attempted.
      Icon selection, alert report-vector lookup, repetition suffix,
      wrapping/colors, adjacent generic unit-summary branch and position.
    alert-hover-two-card-render-region
      reference [0x3fa94d,0x3faf77); classic [0x3f850d,0x3f8b37)
      C status: reference not attempted; classic not attempted.
      Popup/modal gating, both hover-card frames, both occurrences of the
      click instruction, and colored report-row rendering. Additional exits
      are reference 0x3fb44f and classic 0x3f900f.

  This bounded C attempt also failed. Both runs reached the dedicated Java
  script, then the first region exhausted its 60-second decompiler budget:
    reference: Region C unavailable at 0x3d740d: Exception while decompiling
               1403d740d: process: timeout
    classic:   Region C unavailable at 0x3d4fcd: Exception while decompiling
               1403d4fcd: process: timeout
  The thrown exception prevented the other two regions in each image from
  entering the C stage. Both headless shells returned 0 after recording the
  script error; that return code is not C-export success. No region C file
  was produced, and no retry followed. All six original regions and their
  full boundary edges remain available as the precise native UI source.
  All primary message productions, submission/category ownership and popup
  branches below come from completed actual Ghidra C exports. Hover-only
  instruction/count presentation is supported by the native ASM/CFG source;
  it is not represented as a completed C export.

Card/category boundary
  The screenshot is the alert-icon hover card (its instruction begins
  "Left click for recenter and expand options."). The native guest category is
  28 (0x1c). The report-category switch maps only announcement 301 (0x12d,
  GUEST_ARRIVAL) to category 28 in both configured PE files.
  announcement-submit calls this switch and appends the report ID to the
  matching announcement_alertst's +8 vector. The hover owner looks these IDs
  up and uses report.text (+8), rather than rebuilding the visitor sentence.
  The same category reaches the expanded alert popup renderer.
  Category 3 migrant types 49, 50, 69, 70, 71 and 72 share the Reports Arrivals
  tab with category 28, but do not enter this guest hover card. Their producer
  is preserved here as adjacent source evidence, not as extra card branches.
  GUEST_RUMOR (324) in the travellers producer maps to category 30, so its
  rumor/tales sentences and the separate Spoils Report are outside this card.

All guest sentence productions
  Producer: reference 0x10b150..0x1103b0, classic 0x10b0e0..0x110340.
  All six submission sites use descriptor DWORD 0x2012d (type 301, color 2),
  bright 1 and display timer 2000. The complete producer is preserved.

  New visitor, one unit:
    UnitLabel(unit) + " has arrived."
    UnitLabel(unit) + " is visiting."
  New visitors, multiple units with no consistent performance entity:
    one independent record per unit using the same two branches above.
  New visitors, multiple units with a consistent performance entity:
    EntityName(entity) + ", the performance troupe, has arrived."
    EntityName(entity) + ", a performance troupe, is visiting."
  Arrived versus visiting is selected using the unit's historical figure
  lookup, then info pointer +0x130, then its +0x28 information record. All
  three pointers must exist and information record.word0 must be 1 to choose
  arrived; a missing pointer or any other value chooses visiting. For a
  performance troupe the first live unit supplies this information. Zero
  live units produces no new-visitor sentence.

  Returns, one live unit or no returning squad:
    one unit: UnitLabel(unit) + " has returned."
    two units: UnitLabel(first) + " and " + UnitLabel(second)
               + " have returned."
    three or more units: UnitLabel(first) + " and others have returned."
  Returns, multiple live units and returning squads present:
    one squad: SquadLabel(first) + " have returned."
    multiple squads: SquadLabel(first) + " and others have returned."
  The native branch prioritizes the unit form when live-unit count is one,
  even when a squad is also present. Each of these five return productions
  can append the optional history field described below.

Semantic fields, not finite phrase substitutions
  UnitLabel is native unit formatter reference 0x1330c30 / classic 0x132bba0,
  called with its trailing mode argument zero. It supplies the actual name,
  identity, profession/office and transformation fields as a single caption;
  its title-field branches are extracted separately in ../visitor-unit-identity.
  EntityName is reference 0xb92900 / classic 0xb8f940.
  SquadLabel tests actual squad.alias (+0x80) for emptiness. A nonempty alias
  is appended verbatim. Only an empty alias uses squad.name (+8) through
  native EnglishName reference 0xa946e0 / classic 0xa91760. Spelling is not
  evidence of an alias or a reason to translate user-authored names.

Empty semantic fields
  The producer never tests UnitLabel or EntityName output for emptiness. It
  appends the selected fixed suffix and submits the resulting record anyway.
  It also does not test the generated SquadLabel after the empty-alias branch.
  Therefore exact bare productions include " has arrived.", " is visiting.",
  " has returned.", " have returned.", " and others have returned.",
  ", the performance troupe, has arrived." and
  ", a performance troupe, is visiting.". In the two-unit return production,
  either UnitLabel can independently be empty; both empty produce
  " and  have returned." (two spaces between and and have). The optional
  history appendix is still available for these return records. Because a
  fixed suffix remains, announcement-submit's empty-whole-text rejection does
  not suppress them. These exact type-301 paths do not justify accepting an
  empty unit field in unrelated grammars.
  announcement-submit preserves the source case and bytes when copying into
  report+8 (reference 0xe46ad). Its earlier helper 0x52bd30 is only the native
  game-log sink; pe-reference-announcement-text-log-sink.asm retains that
  source without opening any log. There is no capitalization call here.
  The translation-side native_announcement_display_source strips leading
  whitespace and collapses internal whitespace, but preserves case. Thus
  bare forms normalize to lowercase "has arrived.", "is visiting.",
  "has returned.", "have returned.", "and others have returned." and
  "and have returned."; the troupe forms retain their initial comma.

Optional return report appendix
  The return event ID is selected from returning army records -> squad_mission
  -> live units' 64 int32 event slots at unit+0x404. Disagreeing IDs omit the
  report. There is no history-event subtype restriction at this selection.
  An available event is formatted through its virtual +0xd0 slot with native
  flags 0,1,0. If the resulting field is nonempty, exactly two ASCII spaces
  and the entire history sentence are appended to the same return-text owner
  before type 301 submission. An absent event, empty field or no selected ID
  adds no text. This creates an optional appendix for every return family.
  Exact call sites: reference 0x10dbf2/0x10dd99/0x10dfbc;
                    classic 0x10db82/0x10dd29/0x10df4c.
  The complete reachable 133-type virtual dispatch and descendant sources
  are retained in ../announcement-negotiation-native/returned-history-dispatch.tsv.
  This open semantic field must remain delegated to the existing structural
  history-document path; it is not limited to the visitor sentence suffixes.

Hover and expanded-card text
  Hover instruction (both alert-icon and alert-button branches):
    "Left click for recenter and expand options.  Right click to dismiss."
  Expanded category-28 card instruction:
    "You can recenter on certain announcements.  Right click to close."
  The native alternate "Select a report to view the full text.  Right click
  to close." requires report_unid entries. Guest constructors create report
  IDs in +8, not unit-summary entries, so this is a generic UI branch rather
  than an additional guest-caption production.
  Report repetition counter is report+0x34. Zero preserves only report.text;
  positive values append " x" and the decimal value counter+1. Repetition is
  counted by matching complete source report text in announcement-submit,
  and does not alter any UnitLabel, EntityName or SquadLabel field.
  The "Somebody is fighting!/sparring./hunting." summaries belong to other
  alert categories' unit vectors and cannot be supplied by these guest
  constructors. They are present in the complete generic renderer sources
  to make that distinction explicit.

Existing processing boundaries
  Type 301 sentence syntax and history appendices are described in
  ../fortress-arrivals/decompiled-arrival-productions.tsv and handled through
  the existing complete-announcement grammar and native history documents.
  The untranslated generated office title in the supplied screenshot is
  inside UnitLabel, before " is visiting."; adding another visitor suffix
  cannot resolve that title-field failure.
